advisory.finding: _mcnemar — the exact two-sided McNemar test that the ADR explicitly says 'the architecture choice rests on' — has no test, despite being a pure deterministic function. Named violating input: _mcnemar over paired hit vectors with b01=3, b10=13 (n=16) must return p≈0.0213 (the exact value ADR 0122 cites as the sole distinguishable advantage justifying adoption of `vector`); the n==0 concordant case must return p=1.0. dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make digest_document tolerate scalar non-string field values (coerce with str()) so a malformed field degrades to an empty/stringified document rather than raising TypeError.
evidence: evals/similar-tickets/measure.py:431: `doc[field] = value if isinstance(value, str) else " ".join(value)`

`_parse_digest_reply` (line 697-699) coerces every field to str via `str(value)` / join, but `digest_document` is invoked on `record.get("value", record)` (line 451, 436) without that guarantee for arbitrary cached shapes.
dropped.finding: digest_document() assumes every non-None field value is either a str or an iterable of strings; a scalar non-string value (e.g. an int, bool, or nested dict surviving a YAML parse) would make `" ".join(value)` raise TypeError. The cached digests pass through _parse_digest_reply which normalizes fields to str, so committed data is safe, but digest_document is also called directly on record.get('value', record) in rank_digest_bm25f/embed_corpus and would not be protected if a differently-shaped value were ever cached or passed.
scenarios: A future digest reply shape or hand-edited digests.json where a field parses as an int/dict rather than str/list of str.
dropped.suggested_fix: In digest_document, replace `doc[field] = value if isinstance(value, str) else " ".join(value)` with a form that stringifies non-list scalars, mirroring _parse_digest_reply: e.g. `doc[field] = value if isinstance(value, str) else (" ".join(str(v) for v in value) if isinstance(value, list) else str(value))`.
